key_features.classic_presentation: IBD flare presents with CRAMPY ABDOMINAL PAIN and CHRONIC BLOODY DIARRHEA (3-10+ stools/day). Pain is INTERMITTENT, crampy, 5-8/10 severity. Onset is over days to weeks. Patient usually has KNOWN DIAGNOSIS of Crohn's or ulcerative colitis with prior flares. Key associated symptoms: BLOODY or MUCOID diarrhea (hallmark), urgency, tenesmus (feeling of incomplete evacuation), weight loss, fatigue, LOW-GRADE FEVER. Location: Diffuse cramping, or RLQ if Crohn's (terminal ileum). Key history: Diagnosed IBD, missed medications, recent infections, stress. May have extra-intestinal manifestations (joint pain, eye inflammation, skin lesions). Key positives: Blood and mucus in stool, cramping relieved by defecation, chronic/relapsing pattern. Key negatives: Acute onset diarrhea without blood suggests gastroenteritis. First episode of bloody diarrhea needs workup (not assumed to be IBD).

red_flags: Severe abdominal pain with peritoneal signs - toxic megacolon or perforation, call 911
High fever >102°F with tachycardia - severe colitis, toxic megacolon risk
Severe bloody diarrhea with >10 stools/day - severe flare, needs hospitalization
Abdominal distension with decreased bowel sounds - toxic megacolon, surgical emergency
